stem: A team plans a storage clean-up and needs to know how far back the housekeeping command leaves files alone when nobody has tuned the setting. The table carries no custom property for this, and the workspace is on delivered defaults.

option_texts.A: Seven days, which is the default retention threshold for data files
option_texts.B: Zero days, so every unreferenced file goes as soon as the command runs
option_texts.C: Thirty days, matching the period the log files are kept for
option_texts.D: Three hundred and sixty five days, so a full year stays recoverable

drill_answer_short: The default retention threshold for data files after running VACUUM is 7 days
decision_hinge: The default retention threshold for data files after running VACUUM is 7 days, and setting a higher threshold gives access to a greater history while increasing storage costs.

plausible_options.C: how far back the housekeeping command leaves files alone

eliminated_by.B: The table carries no custom property for this
eliminated_by.D: the workspace is on delivered defaults

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - an immediate purge would break readers and time travel
distractor_traps.C: T3: confusable sibling - 30 days is the log file retention, not the data file threshold
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - a year is not any default on the platform

stem: A streaming sink has produced an enormous number of tiny files and read latency has climbed. The table defines partitions, and the team wants to know how the compaction command treats that boundary when it rewrites the layout.

option_texts.A: Compaction ignores partitions and merges files freely across the whole table
option_texts.B: Compaction runs within partitions, grouping the small files inside each one
option_texts.C: Compaction removes the partitions first and then rewrites one flat layout
option_texts.D: Compaction refuses to run until the partitions are dropped from the table

drill_answer_short: For tables with partitions defined, file compaction and data layout are performed within partitions
decision_hinge: For tables with partitions defined, file compaction and data layout are performed within partitions.

plausible_options.A: an enormous number of tiny files and read latency has climbed

eliminated_by.D: how the compaction command treats that boundary when it rewrites the layout

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - merging across the table would break the partition boundary that still defines the layout
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - compaction never drops the partitioning of a table
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - the command runs happily on a partitioned table

stem: A platform team is tired of scheduling its own maintenance notebooks for managed tables in Unity Catalog. They want the platform to decide when layout and statistics work should happen, instead of a fixed weekly window.

option_texts.A: Liquid clustering, which removes the need for any maintenance operation at all
option_texts.B: Predictive optimization, which automatically rewrites queries to avoid maintenance
option_texts.C: Predictive optimization, which automatically runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE
option_texts.D: Auto Loader, which keeps file counts low as it ingests and needs no maintenance

drill_answer_short: Predictive optimization automatically runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM and ANALYZE on managed tables
decision_hinge: Predictive optimization automatically runs OPTIMIZE, VACUUM, and ANALYZE on Unity Catalog managed tables.

plausible_options.A: want the platform to decide when layout and statistics work should happen

eliminated_by.B: tired of scheduling its own maintenance notebooks for managed tables
eliminated_by.D: instead of a fixed weekly window

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - clustering shapes the layout but still relies on maintenance running
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - the feature schedules maintenance operations, it does not rewrite queries
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - an ingestion mechanism does not maintain the table it writes into

stem: Someone removed a managed table from a production schema this morning and the team wants it back without restoring from a backup. Nobody has changed the catalog or schema settings that govern this situation.

option_texts.A: Recreate the table from its definition and reload it from the upstream source
option_texts.B: Raise a support request, since a removal of a managed table is final
option_texts.C: Run a time travel query against the table, which still resolves after removal
option_texts.D: Run UNDROP, which recovers the most recently dropped relation of that name

drill_answer_short: UNDROP recovers the most recently dropped relation of that name, within a 7 day recovery period by default
decision_hinge: By default this command undrops or recovers the most recently dropped relation owned by the user of the given relation name, and by default the feature supports recovering dropped relations within a 7 day recovery period.

plausible_options.A: the team wants it back without restoring from a backup

eliminated_by.B: Nobody has changed the catalog or schema settings that govern this situation
eliminated_by.C: Someone removed a managed table from a production schema this morning

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a rebuild does return the data but throws away the recovery path the platform offers
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - a dropped relation is recoverable for a defined window
distractor_traps.C: T5: common misconception - time travel needs the relation to still exist to be addressed

stem: An engineer is starting a brand new bundle project on a laptop and would rather scaffold it from a template than hand-write the first configuration. The CLI is already installed and authenticated against the workspace.

option_texts.A: Run a bundle init command, which initializes a new bundle using a template
option_texts.B: Run a bundle new command, which creates an empty project in the directory
option_texts.C: Run a bundle create command, which registers the project with the workspace
option_texts.D: Run a bundle deploy command, which writes a starter project from a template on first use

drill_answer_short: databricks bundle init initializes a new bundle using a bundle template
decision_hinge: The bundle init command initializes a new bundle using a bundle template, and templates can be configured to prompt the user for values.

plausible_options.D: would rather scaffold it from a template than hand-write the first configuration

eliminated_by.B: starting a brand new bundle project on a laptop
eliminated_by.C: The CLI is already installed and authenticated against the workspace

distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - there is no bundle new command in the CLI
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - there is no bundle create command in the CLI
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - deploy pushes an existing project and never scaffolds one

stem: An engineer has pushed a feature branch from a Databricks Git folder and now has to get that work onto the default branch. Branch protection means the engineer cannot commit to the default branch directly.

option_texts.A: Use the Git dialog's merge control, the only place a protected branch can be merged
option_texts.B: Open the Git provider's interface and raise a pull request against the default branch
option_texts.C: Ask an administrator to disable branch protection for the length of the merge
option_texts.D: Deploy the bundle to production, which promotes the branch into the default one

drill_answer_short: When you cannot commit to the default branch, raise a pull request in the Git provider's interface
decision_hinge: If you don't have permission to commit to the default branch, create a new branch and use your Git provider's interface to create a pull request and merge it into the default branch.

plausible_options.A: now has to get that work onto the default branch

eliminated_by.C: Branch protection means the engineer cannot commit to the default branch directly
eliminated_by.D: has pushed a feature branch from a Databricks Git folder

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the Git dialog does merge branches, but a protected branch is merged through the provider
distractor_traps.C: T4: breaks a stated requirement - removing the protection defeats the control it exists to apply
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - deploying a bundle moves resources to a workspace, not commits between branches

stem: An auditor is tracing which upstream tables feed a reporting table. One transformation step calls a user defined function, and several tables are only ever referenced inside that function's body. The auditor must know whether the graph can be trusted as complete.

option_texts.A: The graph is complete, because every reference inside a function body is captured
option_texts.B: The graph is incomplete, because functions and the tables they use are excluded altogether
option_texts.C: The graph is incomplete, because lineage is not captured for tables referenced inside a function body
option_texts.D: The graph is complete, because referenced tables are resolved before being recorded

drill_answer_short: UDFs appear in the lineage graph, but lineage is not captured for tables referenced inside a UDF body
decision_hinge: UDFs used to transform data between tables or views are captured in the lineage graph, but lineage is not captured for tables or functions referenced inside a UDF body.

plausible_options.A: several tables are only ever referenced inside that function's body

eliminated_by.B: One transformation step calls a user defined function
eliminated_by.D: The auditor must know whether the graph can be trusted as complete

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - the graph records the function, not what it reads inside itself
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - functions do appear, it is their internal references that are missing
distractor_traps.D: T1: fabricated - no resolution step expands a function body for lineage

stem: A team is reviewing a new project and has to say what shape the bundle's top level configuration file takes before they can lint it in their pipeline. They have the repository in front of them but nobody has opened the file yet.

option_texts.A: A JSON document whose bundle schema ships alongside the CLI release
option_texts.B: A Python module that builds the configuration when the CLI imports it
option_texts.C: A TOML file whose sections name each workspace the project deploys to
option_texts.D: A YAML file that carries mappings such as bundle, resources and targets

drill_answer_short: A bundle's databricks.yml is YAML, holding mappings such as bundle, resources and targets
decision_hinge: The bundle configuration file is written in YAML and contains mappings including the bundle mapping, the resources mapping, and the targets top-level mapping.

plausible_options.A: has to say what shape the bundle's top level configuration file takes

eliminated_by.B: nobody has opened the file yet
eliminated_by.C: before they can lint it in their pipeline

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - a JSON schema does back the format, but the file itself is YAML
distractor_traps.B: T1: fabricated - the configuration is declarative, not generated by importing code
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - no part of the bundle format uses TOML
